cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: Source analysis is a core skill in OCR J198, especially in the Depth Study paper

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: Always consider three elements: content (what it says), provenance (who wrote it, when, why), and context (what else was happening)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: Ancient sources include writers like Herodotus, Thucydides, Livy, Polybius and Plutarch

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: Ancient sources may be biased, incomplete, or written long after events — always note their limitations

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: Modern historians provide interpretation and analysis but also have their own perspectives and biases

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: Utility means how useful a source is for answering a specific question — not whether it is true or reliable

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: A source can be useful even if biased — bias itself reveals attitudes and values

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: Cross-referencing sources strengthens arguments by showing where sources agree or disagree

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: When asked about a source's usefulness, consider both what it tells you and what it leaves out

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: Archaeological evidence (inscriptions, coins, pottery, buildings) complements literary sources

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: The Depth Study paper requires you to use sources as evidence to support arguments

cards.front: Recall a key point about Source Analysis Skills
cards.back: Never accept a source at face value — always question its purpose and perspective

cards.front: What should you know about gcse ancient history exam tips — source analysis skills?
cards.back: 1. For Source Analysis Skills, include specific factual detail: dates, names, events and statistics where relevant 2. For source questions, analyse provenance (who, when, why, audience) before using the content 3. In evaluation questions, discuss multiple factors and weigh their relative significance 4. Always link back to the question focus — don't just narrate what happened with Source Analysis Skills 5. Use phrases like 'the most significant factor was... because...' to show analytical judgement
